newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil down sharply on crude, slack demand.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil down sharply on crude, slack demand.

text.p: NWE cracked fuel oil was knocked sharply lower on Thursday on the back of weaker crude, good supplies of Russian straight-run and continued lacklustre end-user buying.
Physical activity was quiet as players waiting for the market to settle.

Some dealers felt the downward spiral would be short-lived. Russian flow is expected to diminish, storage material, both in ARA tanks and end-user stocks, is thinning and winter is approaching. Others saw the drop as a welcome correction to a market getting overheated. High sulphur barges traded between $115-117 fob ARA for much of the day.
Cargoes were pegged as low as $110-112 fob NWE by some traders. Others conceded the market was weaker but felt the level was closer to $120 cif NWE.

Low sulphur cargoes were also quiet with port congestion in Milazzo seemingly knocking out the main Med buyer. As with high sulphur, direction had to be taken from swaps with wet prices pegged at $122-124 fob NWE. A large cargo was understood sold to a trader by a major today although no price was disclosed.
